prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm operations and maintenance system spans offshore/shore assets, personnel, communications, cybersecurity, fire protection, backup power through Grid Interface Relay; excludes public grid/unrelated port operations. Objectives: safety, reliability, integrity, availability, environmental protection. Aliases: Glassfin=Turbine Controller; Morrowick=Offshore Substation; Pale Lantern=Weather Service; Juniper Vale=SCADA Gateway; Thistle Crown=Maintenance Planning Engine; Amber Quay=Shore Control Room; Kestrel Bay=Crew Transfer Vessel; Sable Orchard=Fleet Dispatch Console; Mosslight=Warehouse System; Copper Finch=Metocean Buoy; Quiet Harbor=Cybersecurity Gateway. Turbine Controller controls turbines, produces Pitch Deviation Notice; equipment: Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone inspects blades. Offshore Substation collects/switches power via Main Transformer; Export Cable Monitor monitors export. Duty Planner uses Field Supervisor/Maintenance Planning Engine input; Field Supervisor coordinates offshore work/reports progress changes. HSE Officer verifies safety/responsibilities. Shore Control Room/Control Engineer oversee operations. Marine Coordinator uses Fleet Dispatch Console; Vessel Master retains navigation/transfer authority. Accountable handoffs separate dispatch, marine judgment, supervision, stores. Warehouse System/Storekeeper manage stock/Spares Hub replenishment; Port Agent coordinates port access/cargo. Transport: Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel, Helideck. Accountability: Personnel Tracking Console, North Access Scanner, South Access Scanner; authorization: Work Permit Portal. Metocean Buoy measures wind/waves/current/temperature/pressure; logger timestamps/retains history offline. Require exposure-resistant sensors, configured intervals/thresholds, routine synchronization/health checks. Weather Service validates observations, produces Squall Window Bulletin; Weather Analyst advises access/work limitations. Vessel AIS Receiver produces Position Quality Flag on failed integrity/low confidence; recipients unspecified. Weather Hold requires safe-resumption confirmation. Cybersecurity Gateway: approved protocols/destinations/accounts only; deny-default external connectivity, documented exceptions; authenticated role-based administration; time-limited/logged/reviewed privilege; protected logs, segmentation/restoration. Cybersecurity Analyst monitors events; boundary loss restricts remote administration without bypassing local protection. SCADA Gateway/SCADA Engineer retain supervisory scope. Lifecycle: verified commissioning; validated routine operation; risk/resource-aware maintenance; refurbishment; safe decommissioning/record transfer. Require accountability, pollution prevention, minimal

New part:
S121: Interfaces are tested after configuration changes to confirm that permitted functions remain available and prohibited paths remain blocked.
S122: Operational procedures identify the authority for approving access, responding to alarms, and returning affected services to normal operation.
S123: This section describes turbine control and remote observation during offshore operations.
S124: Vessel AIS Receiver is designated Blue Granite for this operational concept.
S125: Blade Inspection Drone is designated Larkspur for this operational concept.
S126: Duty Planner prepares the Transfer Manifest Addendum to capture approved vessel deployment changes.
S127: Glassfin adjusts turbine output within approved operating limits and blocks commands that conflict with active protection conditions.
S128: Pale Lantern issues forecast updates that support timing decisions for remote observation and field work.
S129: Turbine Controller executes authorized control actions and reports its operating state through established control interfaces.
S130: Pitch System changes blade angle in response to turbine control commands and local protection logic.
S131: Converter Cabinet manages electrical conversion while observing equipment limits and protective interlocks.
S132: Nacelle Condition Monitor provides equipment measurements for ongoing assessment of turbine health.
S133: SCADA Gateway presents turbine status and control availability to authorized shore personnel.
S134: Shore Control Room provides a staffed location for supervisory control and operational review.
S135: Control Engineer reviews alarms and operating conditions before issuing a remote command.
S136: Remote commands are subject to role-based authorization and are recorded for later operational review.
S137: Local protection functions retain priority when remote requests conflict with safe operating limits.
S138: Control availability is checked before remote operation begins and after relevant configuration changes.
S139: Vessel AIS Receiver collects vessel position broadcasts to support marine traffic awareness.
S140: The receiver maintains a time-stamped view of nearby vessel movements when broadcast coverage is available.
S141: Marine Coordinator uses the available traffic picture to support coordination of offshore movements.
S142: Blade Inspection Drone captures close-range visual observations of accessible blade surfaces.
S143: Blade Specialist plans inspection passes to provide consistent coverage of areas selected for examination.
S144: Captured imagery is reviewed for visible surface changes and potential maintenance concerns.
S145: Field Supervisor considers remote observations alongside site conditions before recommending follow-up work.
S146: Drone operation is suspended when weather, visibility, or equipment status makes flight unsafe.
S147: Remote observations supplement field assessment and do not replace required physical inspections.
S148: Maintenance Planning Engine can use reviewed condition information when prioritizing future maintenance activities.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
